dicas.texto: Você está indo muito bem! Para comparar frações com denominadores diferentes, o que acontece se tentarmos encontrar um denominador comum ou olhar para a posição relativa de cada marca em relação à metade da reta (0,5)?
Tente observar a distância de cada marca até o zero. Qual delas está mais próxima do final da reta (o número 1)?
Dica: 3/10 é um pouco menos que 3/9 (ou 1/3). Tente visualizar onde 1/3 estaria se você dividisse a reta em 30 partes iguais para comparar as duas frações.
Pense assim: Se você transformar 1/3 em uma fração com denominador 30, ela vira 10/30. Se transformar 3/10 em denominador 30, ela vira 9/30. Qual é maior, 9/30 ou 10/30?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Mile Bathany swam" e "Mile John swam"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Coach should choose Bethany."; "Coach should choose John."; "Both are equally matched!"; botão Hint; botão Done. dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the number line?
Use the denominator of Bethany's fraction to decide how many equal intervals the line needs.
Look at the bottom number in 3/... and enter that number in Bethany's denominator field.
Count the equal intervals needed to represent tenths, then enter that count and confirm it.
How does a fraction show a location between 0 and 1?
Start at 0, use the denominator to identify the equal intervals, and move forward by the numerator.
On Bethany's line, count three equal intervals to the right from 0.
Click the point reached after three tenth-sized intervals and confirm the fraction shown by the line.
What does the denominator represent when a whole is divided into equal parts?
Read the denominator of John's fraction and use it as the number of equal intervals.
Look at the bottom number in 1/3 and enter it in John's denominator field.
Divide the whole line into thirds, enter the number of equal intervals, and confirm the setting.
How can you locate one equal part of a whole on a number line?
Use the denominator to identify the size of each interval, then count the intervals indicated by the numerator.
Starting at 0, move one equal interval to the right on John's line.
Click the first division after 0 and confirm the fraction represented by that location.
On number lines with the same whole, which swimmer's point is farther to the right?
Compare the two marked locations on the number lines rather than comparing only the numerators.
Look closely at the two marked points between 0 and 1 and identify which one is farther from 0.
Select the option naming the swimmer whose marked fraction represents the greater distance.
How can you tell that a fraction is less than one whole?
Compare each numerator with its denominator and check that the marked point lies between 0 and 1.
For both fractions, verify that the top number is smaller than the bottom number.
Confirm that both marked points are before 1, then press Done to submit the completed comparison.

exercicio.statement:
Bethany and John's coach needs to pick a fast swimmer for a certain competition. The coach told each of them to swim a mile. After some time has passed, the coach decided to check on their progress. Use the number line to help the coach see who has swum more.
Bethany swam 3/10 of a mile.
John swam 1/3 of a mile.
Who should the coach pick for the competition?

Look at the bottom number in 3/... and enter that number in Bethany's denominator field.
Count the equal intervals needed to represent tenths, then enter that count and confirm it.

misconceptions.description: Aluno troca as retas ou os denominadores entre os atletas
misconceptions.feedback: Check which fraction belongs to Bethany. Her denominator is the bottom number in 3/10, and it tells you how many equal parts Bethany's line needs.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde o número de marcas necessárias para dividir o segmento com o número de intervalos
misconceptions.feedback: You counted marks instead of intervals. The denominator tells you the number of equal spaces between 0 and 1, not the number of boundary marks.

hints.message: How does a fraction show a location between 0 and 1?
Start at 0, use the denominator to identify the equal intervals, and move forward by the numerator.
On Bethany's line, count three equal intervals to the right from 0.
Click the point reached after three tenth-sized intervals and confirm the fraction shown by the line.

nodes.description: Set John's number line to the correct number of equal parts.

hints.message: What does the denominator represent when a whole is divided into equal parts?
Read the denominator of John's fraction and use it as the number of equal intervals.
Look at the bottom number in 1/3 and enter it in John's denominator field.
Divide the whole line into thirds, enter the number of equal intervals, and confirm the setting.

misconceptions.description: Aluno troca as retas ou os denominadores entre os atletas
misconceptions.feedback: Check which fraction belongs to John. His denominator is the bottom number in 1/3, so John's line must use that number of equal parts.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde o número de marcas necessárias para dividir o segmento com o número de intervalos
misconceptions.feedback: You counted boundary marks instead of equal intervals. To divide the line into thirds, count the spaces, not the endpoints and cuts together.

nodes.description: Mark John's distance at 1/3 on his number line.
nodes.instruction: Mark John's distance at 1/3 on his number line.

hints.message: How can you locate one equal part of a whole on a number line?
Use the denominator to identify the size of each interval, then count the intervals indicated by the numerator.
Starting at 0, move one equal interval to the right on John's line.
Click the first division after 0 and confirm the fraction represented by that location.

hints.message: On number lines with the same whole, which swimmer's point is farther to the right?
Compare the two marked locations on the number lines rather than comparing only the numerators.
Look closely at the two marked points between 0 and 1 and identify which one is farther from 0.
Select the option naming the swimmer whose marked fraction represents the greater distance.

hints.message: How can you tell that a fraction is less than one whole?
Compare each numerator with its denominator and check that the marked point lies between 0 and 1.
For both fractions, verify that the top number is smaller than the bottom number.
Confirm that both marked points are before 1, then press Done to submit the completed comparison.
